purpose: reader-facing explanation of the five evidence sources used to research the AI Engineer role

required_facts.fact: The AI Engineer role depends on company, team, and problem, producing inconsistent and sometimes contradictory expectations.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 3-6: role instability and market-shaping factors are described.

required_facts.fact: The first research source was Alexey's more than 15 years of ML and AI industry experience and his teaching at AI Engineering Buildcamp.
required_facts.evidence: Source line 30: personal experience source is specified.

required_facts.fact: The second source was more than 1,500 job postings collected over three months from several major cities.
required_facts.evidence: Source line 39: job-posting dataset size, time range, and locations are stated.

required_facts.fact: The job-posting dataset was used to study role names, responsibilities, repeated skills and tools, and overlap with ML Engineer positions.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 43-50: dataset questions and presentation focus are listed.

required_facts.fact: The third source was Twitter/X and Reddit interview stories, with research-agent help including Grok analysis of X posts.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 52-59: social sources, agent assistance, and their value are described.

required_facts.fact: The fourth source was planned direct conversations with hiring managers, community members, and engineers working in AI Engineering.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 61-74: conversation groups and public/private use are specified.

required_facts.fact: Social stories and direct conversations were intended to inform a session about interview structure, evaluation criteria, and hiring decisions.
required_facts.evidence: Source line 76: combined purpose of sources three and four is stated.

required_facts.fact: The fifth source was around 60 public GitHub repositories containing take-home assignment solutions.
required_facts.evidence: Source line 81: repository dataset is specified.

required_facts.fact: Deep research agents from Google and OpenAI did not reliably find 100 repositories and sometimes hallucinated additional results.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 83-87: limitations and useful query-generation role are listed.

required_facts.fact: The final repository workflow used agents to craft stronger queries and manual review and aggregation for local analysis.
required_facts.evidence: Source line 89: hybrid workflow is stated.

author_attribution: Explain the five-source research plan as Alexey documented it, retaining the differences in reliability and purpose among the sources.
